## Why Reproducibility Matters

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
### The Reproducibility Crisis

-   70%+ of researchers have failed to reproduce another's work
-   50%+ have failed to reproduce their *own* work
-   Retractions increasing exponentially
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
### Our Solution

-   Version control (Git)
-   Package management (renv)
-   Pipeline automation (targets)
-   Literate programming (Quarto)
:::
:::::

::: {.fragment}
![xkcd: Replication Crisis](../images/xkcd-replication-crisis.png){fig-alt="xkcd comic about the replication crisis - researchers trying to reproduce reproduction crisis studies" width="50%"}

::: {.aside}
xkcd #3117
:::

## Git & GitHub

### Why Version Control?

-   **Track changes**: See exactly what changed when
-   **Collaborate**: Multiple people, same codebase
-   **Backup**: Your work lives in the cloud
-   **Submission**: GitHub Classroom for assignments

::: fragment
### Basic Workflow

``` bash
git clone <repo-url>    # Copy repo to local
git add .               # Stage changes
git commit -m "message" # Save snapshot
git push                # Upload to GitHub
```
:::

## Git Mental Model

### The 4 Commands You'll Use 90% of the Time

| Command | What It Does | Analogy |
|---------|--------------|---------|
| `git add .` | Stage changes | "I want to save these" |
| `git commit -m "msg"` | Record snapshot | "Here's what I did" |
| `git pull` | Get updates | "What did others do?" |
| `git push` | Send to GitHub | "Share my work" |

::: fragment
**Pro tip:** Write commit messages that explain *why*, not just *what*.

❌ "Updated code"

✅ "Fix power calculation to use correct sample size formula"
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## When Git Goes Wrong

::: {.callout-tip}
## Don't Panic
Everyone messes up Git. The good news: almost everything is recoverable.
:::

### Your Rescue Resource

**[ohshitgit.com](https://ohshitgit.com/)** — Solutions for common Git disasters

### Common Issues

| Problem | Quick Fix |
|---------|-----------|
| Committed to wrong branch | `git reset HEAD~1` then re-commit |
| Need to undo last commit | `git reset --soft HEAD~1` |
| Merge conflict | Edit file, remove `<<<<` markers, commit |
| Pushed sensitive data | Contact me immediately |

## Clean Code Principles

### Definition

> "Clean code is **easy to understand**, **easy to modify**, and hence **easy to debug**."

### The Gentzkow-Shapiro Rules

1. **Abstract to eliminate redundancy** — DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself)
2. **Abstract to improve clarity** — Name things well
3. **Otherwise, don't abstract** — Simplicity wins

::: fragment
### The Dishwasher Analogy

A dishwasher user needs to know:

- How to load dishes
- Which button to press

They don't need to understand the plumbing or electrical wiring.

**Your functions should work the same way.**
:::

### Professional Standards

-   **Unit testing** = "what washing hands are to surgeons"
-   **Code review** improves quality and spreads knowledge
-   **Documentation** = gift to your future self

### For This Course

::: {.callout-tip}
## Encouraged Practices
-   **Pair programming** on problem sets
-   **README files** as project landing pages
-   **Commit often** with meaningful messages
:::

::: fragment
### Remember

> Your most important collaborator is **future you** — six months from now, trying to remember why the code works.
:::

## Package Management with renv

### The Problem

``` r
# Works on your machine...
install.packages("dplyr")  # Version 1.1.4

# Breaks on mine...
# I have dplyr 0.8.3
```

::: fragment
### The Solution: renv

``` r
# First time setup (already done in templates)
renv::init()

# Restore packages (you run this)
renv::restore()

# After adding packages
renv::snapshot()
```
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Pipeline Automation with targets

### Why targets?

-   Only re-run what changed
-   Document dependencies automatically
-   Scale to complex analyses

::: fragment
### Basic Structure

``` r
# _targets.R
list(
  tar_target(raw_data, read_csv("data/raw.csv")),
  tar_target(clean_data, clean_fn(raw_data)),
  tar_target(model, fit_model(clean_data)),
  tar_target(results, summarize(model))
)
```
:::

::: callout-tip
We'll use targets for the capstone project. Labs use simpler structure.
:::

## Literate Programming with Quarto

### Code + Narrative = Reproducible Report

``` markdown
## Methods

We estimate the treatment effect using:

`​``{r}
model <- lm_robust(outcome ~ treatment, data = df)
`​``

The estimated effect is 0.42.
```

::: fragment
**Output:** A document where code, results, and interpretation live together.
:::

## Your Computing Environment

### Two-Tier Architecture

| Tier            | Platform                 | When to Use                    |
|-----------------|--------------------------|--------------------------------|
| **Primary**     | GitHub Codespaces        | Labs, code-alongs, assignments |
| **Alternative** | Local (Positron/RStudio) | Capstone, offline work         |

::: callout-note
## Zero Local Setup Required

GitHub Codespaces runs a full RStudio Server in your browser. No installation needed!
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Live Demo: GitHub Codespaces

Let's walk through:

1.  Accept assignment via GitHub Classroom link
2.  Click "Open in Codespace" → VS Code opens in browser
3.  Choose your IDE (VS Code or RStudio via port 8787)
4.  Run `renv::restore()` to install packages
5.  Work on your code
6.  Commit and push when done — no download needed

::: notes
Walk through the demo slowly. Pause for questions. This is where students often get stuck.
:::
